docs.title: Burble
docs.text:
Burble is an open-source worldbuilding platform built around a rigorous ontology.

It is designed to support:

  • Deep, consistent worldbuilding
  • Story and campaign tracking
  • TTRPG play
  • Future live game / simulation layers

docs.title: Core Ideas
docs.text:
• Ontology Layer — What exists and what is true in the world
  • Story Layer — Narrative structure that references the ontology
  • State Layer — Live mechanical and situational state
  • Composites — User-friendly facades (Culture, Economy, Ecology, etc.) over the formal ontology

docs.title: Services Overview
docs.text: Burble is split into focused services:

docs.title: Ontology Service
docs.text: Authoritative source of world definition and long-lived truth. Owns formal archetypes, statements, and composite mappings.

docs.title: Story Service
docs.text: Narrative structure (campaigns, sessions, scenes, arcs). References ontology entities but does not own world truth.

docs.title: State Service
docs.text: Live mechanical and situational state (HP, inventory, conditions, positions, etc.). Shields the Ontology service from high-frequency updates. Promotes significant changes back to the Ontology at save points.

docs.title: TTRPG / Game Service(s)
docs.text: Rules, resolution, and play experience. Primarily reads and writes to the State service.

docs.title: Formal Archetypes
docs.text: These are the only first-class types in the ontology.

docs.title: Concrete
docs.text: Archetype Description Character Named cognizant entity (can want, know, decide) Item Non-cognizant thing that can be moved as a whole Location Fixed spatial extent at any scale Substance Material or elemental composition

docs.title: Collective
docs.text: Archetype Description Organization Collective treated as a single unit Species Inherent category of being Lineage Specific hereditary line

docs.title: Temporal
docs.text: Archetype Description Event Occurrence with a before and after Period Temporal extent that contains events Instance Single point in time

docs.title: Attributive
docs.text: Archetype Description Action Reusable capability to do something Trait Passive capacity, condition, or status Title Socially recognized standing that can be transferred

docs.title: Abstract & Structural
docs.text: Archetype Description System Framework of interacting rules and structures Worldview Religion, philosophy, ideology, or belief system Concept Information that can be known, shared, or kept secret Logic Definitional fact that constrains what is possible Rule Constraint that exists by decree or agreement (can be broken)

docs.title: Classification Guide
docs.text: This guide is used by both humans and AI agents to decide which formal archetype(s) an entity should receive.

docs.title: Primary Decision Tree
docs.text:
1. Time-related?

    • Span of time → Period
    • Single occurrence → Event
    • Exact moment → Instance

  2. Physical / Spatial?

    • Has agency → Character
    • Movable as a whole → Item
    • Fixed place → Location
    • Material composition → Substance

  3. Group or Category of Being?

    • Collective unit → Organization
    • Inherent kind of being → Species
    • Hereditary line → Lineage

  4. Capability or Standing?

    • Something done → Action
    • Something possessed → Trait
    • Transferable social standing → Title

  5. Abstract / Structural?

    • Interacting framework → System
    • Belief / value system → Worldview
    • Knowable information → Concept
    • Hard law of reality → Logic
    • Breakable decree/agreement → Rule

docs.title: Multi-Archetype Guidance
docs.text: An entity may legitimately receive more than one archetype when it strongly satisfies multiple tests (e.g. Lineage + Organization, Item + Character).

docs.title: Composites
docs.text: Composites are user-facing concepts that sit on top of the formal ontology. They have real API endpoints and can be used as if they were first-class, but internally they map to formal archetypes.

docs.title: Core Composites
docs.text:
Composite Primary Archetype(s) Common Supporting Archetypes Culture Worldview Organization, Species, Concept, Rule Religion Worldview Organization, Concept, Rule, Character Economy System Rule, Substance, Title, Organization Ecology Location + Species Substance, System Technology System Item, Action, Logic, Substance Magic System System Logic, Action, Substance, Rule Language System or Concept Worldview, Concept Government Organization + System Title, Rule, Worldview Cosmology Location + Logic + Worldview Concept, Period

Composites exist so that users can work with familiar concepts while the system maintains a clean and rigorous underlying model.

docs.title: Ontology Overview
docs.text:
The Burble Ontology models world state: what exists, what is true, and when it was true.

Narrative structures (plots, arcs, scenes) belong in the separate Story layer.

docs.title: Two-Layer Design
docs.text:
1. Formal Archetypes The real, stored types. Used for persistence, querying, relationships, and AI classification.

  2. Composites User-facing concepts (Culture, Economy, Ecology, etc.). These are facades that map onto one or more formal archetypes.

This separation keeps the core model clean while matching how worldbuilders naturally think.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• Nodes are nouns; statements are verbs
  • An entity may have multiple archetypes
  • Entities can change archetypes over time
  • Time lives on statements, not on entities
  • Composites are abstractions over the formal model
